comparison: Both address the same claims (C3, C4, C34-C36, C39, C41-C42, C44) about ExoIII's ssDNase activity demonstrated with FQ reporters. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with systematic experimental data and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, questioning substrate design (whether ExoIII interacts with fluorophore ends affecting quenching), challenging the characterization as 'highly active' by noting 'quantitative activity is in fact very low,' and noting 'some aspects remain incomplete.'

Both address claims C45-C51 about directional degradation and kinetic measurements from gel electrophoresis. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with comprehensive time-course data and appropriate controls, though notes calculation methodology could be more explicit. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'technical approaches' as a strength and 'solid evidence for ssDNA nuclease activity.'

Both address claims C56-C65 about mass spectrometry evidence for exo- and endonuclease activities. OpenEval finds C56-C64 SUPPORTED but C65 (sequence-specific activation) speculative. Peer reviewers find these SUPPORTED without challenging the mass spectrometry data or interpretation, with editor noting 'solid evidence for ssDNA nuclease activity.'

Both address identical claims C67-C72 about reaction conditions, Mg2+ dependence, temperature effects, and kinetics. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with systematic experimental data. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, not challenging the biochemical characterizations, with editor acknowledging 'solid evidence.'

Both address identical claims C73-C76 about sequence-dependent inhibition by poly-G sequences. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by convergent mass spectrometry and homopolymeric substrate evidence, though mechanism remains speculative. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED without challenge, encompassed in editor's 'solid evidence' statement.

Both address claims C77-C82 about commercial kit performance and probe degradation. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with appropriate controls, though notes actual detection impact needs validation. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, with editor explicitly noting 'a strength of the manuscript is the testing of popular kits... and coming up with and testing practical solutions.'

OpenEval R7 addresses C83-C88 about SSB/T4 gp32 protection and in vivo roles. Peer R6 addresses overlapping claims C83, C85-C87 about SSB protection. Both find the protection data SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C88 (in vivo regulatory roles) is speculative. Peer reviewers support the practical solutions including SSB proteins without challenging these findings.

Both address claims C89-C95 about mutagenesis identifying critical residues and shared active center. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with systematic mutagenesis data and consistency with structural studies. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, with editor explicitly stating the manuscript 'identifies residues that contribute to it [ssDNA nuclease activity].'

Both address claims C53-C54 about structural differences between ExoIII and APE1 (αM helix deterioration). OpenEval finds C53-C54 SUPPORTED but C55 (evolutionary adaptation) highly speculative. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, specifically asking whether mutational analysis supports the hypothesis about the αM helix's role in substrate specificity differences.

Both address claims C96-C99, C103-C106 about R170A mutant's differential activity profile. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED though mechanistic interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, encompassed in editor's acknowledgment that the manuscript 'identifies residues that contribute to it.'

OpenEval R9 addresses C96-C97 about K121A mutant replacing wild-type in applications. Peer R10 addresses the same claims. OpenEval finds these reasonable but requiring validation in actual detection assays. Peer reviewers find these SUPPORTED, with editor explicitly noting 'a strength... coming up with and testing practical solutions (e.g.,... ExoIII variants such as K121A).'

Both address claims C107-C117 about the mechanistic model for ssDNA recognition. OpenEval finds these UNCERTAIN, noting the model is internally consistent but largely speculative, lacking direct structural evidence. Peer reviewers are also UNCERTAIN, with editor noting 'some aspects in the study remain incomplete' and one reviewer questioning whether substrate design 'would represent real ssDNA activity.'

Both address claims C120-C127 about dsDNA substrates with 3' ssDNA overhangs and length-dependent effects. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with clear experimental data, though biological role and practical suggestions need validation. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED without challenge, encompassed in editor's 'solid evidence' statement.

Both address claims C130-C134 about fork and bubble structures. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with experimental data and T4 gp32 protection experiments, though biological significance (C135) is speculative. Peer reviewers also find these SUPPORTED, with editor acknowledging 'solid evidence' and practical solutions including SSB proteins.

OpenEval R13 addresses C136-C141 including C140 about mutant applications. Peer R10 addresses C96-C97, C140 about mutant applications. OpenEval finds recommendations logical but lacking validation in diagnostic applications. Peer reviewers find mutant applications SUPPORTED, with editor noting this as 'a strength of the manuscript.'

Both address C52 comparing ExoIII to ExoI. OpenEval finds this UNCERTAIN, noting no direct comparative data is presented and biological significance is speculative. Peer reviewers are also UNCERTAIN, with one reviewer stating 'the work is of low interest with regard to biology' and editor noting 'some aspects remain incomplete.'

OpenEval R14 addresses C55 about evolutionary adaptation of APE1. Peer R15 addresses biological significance claims including C55. OpenEval finds C55 highly speculative lacking supporting evidence. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with one reviewer directly challenging biological significance claims stating 'the work is of low interest with regard to biology.'

Both address biological implications and future directions (C143-C144 in OpenEval R16, included in broader biological claims in Peer R15). OpenEval finds these UNCERTAIN as speculative extrapolations from in vitro data. Peer reviewers are also UNCERTAIN, challenging biological significance and noting 'some aspects remain incomplete.'

OpenEval R7 addresses C88 about in vivo regulatory roles of SSB proteins. Peer R15 addresses biological significance claims including C88. OpenEval notes C88 is speculative but reasonable based on in vitro data. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN about biological claims, with one reviewer stating 'the work is of low interest with regard to biology.'

OpenEval R12 addresses C135 about biological significance of fork/bubble digestion. Peer R15 addresses biological significance claims including C135. OpenEval notes C135 is speculative requiring in vivo validation. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, challenging biological significance claims and noting incomplete aspects.

OpenEval R2 includes C66 about comparative analysis with dsDNA substrates. Peer R3 also includes C66 in mass spectrometry findings. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes comprehensive comparative analysis; peer reviewers acknowledge 'solid evidence for ssDNA nuclease activity' encompassing these findings.

Peer R14 addresses C37-C38 about comparative nuclease activity data presentation. Reviewer requests better visualization to evaluate comparative claims, finding current presentation unclear. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically addresses these comparative data presentation claims.
